built: A replay set in this repository, never shipped: a script Sal starts that runs orbit's six default lifecycle commands (explore, propose, apply, the system review, the walk, archive) as real billed Claude Code sessions, each in a small throwaway project prepared at the state just before that command, three times each by default, and grades every session only by what orbit itself printed or wrote. A second script compares two such runs and says whether a cut is no worse than the baseline. The checks that cost nothing run in npm test. CI now also checks the generated skills with Claude Code's own validator, pinned to one version.
seams: Each billed run asks Sal to type the model and a total cost ceiling, and refuses to start without them; it never starts a session that could take the spend past that ceiling. The CI build now fails when Claude Code's validator reports an error or a warning in a generated skill.
deviations: Two of the stage's exit criteria wait on Sal's billed runs: each case shown failing on a deliberately broken body, and the baseline recorded with its cost. Against the proposal: the cheap first run's ceiling is $8, not $3, because the runner sets aside each case's whole budget (up to $4) before starting it; and the free checks also show every grader passing on the state its command leaves, which the proposal did not ask for.
detail: replay/run.mjs, replay/compare.mjs, replay/lib/ (build, fixture, trace, graders, seed helpers), replay/shim/orbit, replay/project/, six cases under replay/cases/ seeded only through orbit emit and orbit new change, test/replay/ (runner, cases, compare: 34 tests, shown able to fail by four mutations), scripts/validate-skills.mjs with the validate:skills npm script and a failing CI step on the Linux leg.
